Definition: from a compound of G4253 and G3708; to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect:--keep (with a garrison). Compare G5083.
BiblicalUsage: Phroureo means to guard, to keep watch, to mount guard over something, and it is the word for God's keeping of His people. Peter says believers are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation, and Paul says the peace of God shall keep our hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. Before faith came, he says, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed, and the governor under Aretas kept the city of Damascus with a garrison to take Paul.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe phroureo is the picture of God's protection: a garrison around a city, a guard over a heart, a power keeping a soul unto salvation. The law kept us shut up until faith came, and now the peace of God keeps what the law could not. My position is that I am not kept by my own strength but by God's garrison, and the peace that guards my heart is stronger than any wall.
